title: Python Module Not Found
explanation: Python runtime cannot locate the imported package or module within sys.path or the active virtual environment.
possible_causes: The dependency is not installed in the active virtual environment
The command executed against the global Python interpreter rather than a virtual environment
Typo in module or package import name
Missing __init__.py in a local directory intended as a Python package
diagnostic_checks: Check active environment using 'which python' or 'Get-Command python'
Verify installed packages using 'pip list' or 'poetry show'
Inspect sys.path from Python interactive shell
suggested_resolutions: Activate the project virtual environment before running the command
Install the missing dependency via 'pip install <module_name>' or pyproject.toml
Verify working directory or PYTHONPATH contains the package root

title: Python Circular or Invalid Import
explanation: The module was located successfully, but the requested symbol or attribute does not exist within it or is not yet available due to circular dependencies.
possible_causes: Circular import between two interdependent modules
A local file shares the same name as a standard library or third-party module (shadowing)
The requested symbol was deprecated, renamed, or moved in the installed library version
Typo in the imported attribute or class name
diagnostic_checks: Check if any local file (e.g. email.py, requests.py) shadows an installed module
Examine call trace for circular import cycles (module A imports B which imports A)
Check library version and exported symbols via 'dir(module)'
suggested_resolutions: Rename shadowing local files or packages
Refactor circular dependencies by deferring imports inside functions or splitting shared types
Update import path to match the installed library version's API

title: Python Attribute Access on NoneType
explanation: Attempted to access a field, method, or property on an object that evaluated to None at runtime.
possible_causes: A function that returns None implicitly or explicitly had its return value chained
A database query, dictionary lookup, or API search returned no record (empty result)
An uninitialized instance variable was accessed before assignment
diagnostic_checks: Check where the variable received its value immediately prior to the failing line
Verify whether database queries or API calls returned an expected record
Inspect if an in-place modifying method (e.g. list.sort()) returned None
suggested_resolutions: Add a guard clause or check 'if obj is not None:' before accessing attributes
Provide a fallback default or raise a descriptive custom error earlier
Do not assign the return value of in-place mutator methods

error_pattern: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for <op>: '<type1>' and '<type2>'
title: Python Unsupported Operand Type
explanation: An arithmetic, bitwise, or concatenation operator was applied between incompatible types (e.g. str and int).
possible_causes: Input data parsed from JSON, CLI, or environment variables remained a string
Implicit assumption that a value was numeric when it was None or string
Operator precedence misunderstanding
diagnostic_checks: Inspect the runtime types using 'type(var)' or logging
Check data coercion at API boundaries or environment parsing
suggested_resolutions: Explicitly convert types using int(), float(), or str() where appropriate
Validate inputs at domain boundaries using Pydantic schemas or type checks
Ensure None values are handled with sensible defaults

title: Python Dictionary Key Error
explanation: Direct subscript lookup dict['key'] failed because the requested key does not exist in the dictionary.
possible_causes: Optional field omitted from an API response or configuration dictionary
Typo or casing mismatch in the dictionary key
Accessing a key before population in an asynchronous or multi-step workflow
diagnostic_checks: Inspect dict.keys() at the point of failure
Verify casing of keys (e.g. 'authorization' vs 'Authorization')
suggested_resolutions: Use dict.get('key_name', default) instead of direct subscript indexing
Check existence using 'if key in my_dict:' before access
Validate dictionary payloads against strict Pydantic models

error_pattern: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<path>'
title: Python File Not Found
explanation: An operation attempted to open or read a file at a path that does not exist relative to the current working directory.
possible_causes: Relative path evaluated from a different current working directory than expected
File path typo or incorrect path separator between OS environments
File has not yet been generated by an upstream build or export step
diagnostic_checks: Print os.getcwd() to inspect the actual execution directory
Check os.path.exists(path) with both relative and absolute paths
suggested_resolutions: Construct paths relative to the current file using pathlib.Path(__file__).parent
Use pathlib.Path for cross-platform slash normalization
Ensure prerequisite files are created before dependent execution steps

error_pattern: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '<property>')
title: JavaScript Property Access on Undefined
explanation: Attempted to access a property or invoke a method on an object reference that is currently undefined or null.
possible_causes: Component rendered before asynchronous network fetch completed
Optional nested field missing in API payload
Function parameter omitted or passed without expected default object
diagnostic_checks: Log the parent object before the access site or inspect with debugger
Check network request timing and loading state indicators in UI components
suggested_resolutions: Use optional chaining: obj?.<property>
Add default values to destructuring: const { <property> = [] } = obj || {}
Render conditionally behind a loading guard: if (!obj) return <Spinner />

title: JavaScript .map() Called on Non-Array
explanation: Attempted to call the Array.prototype.map() method on an object, string, null, or undefined value.
possible_causes: API returned an error object or single item instead of an expected list
State was initialized with null or undefined rather than an empty array []
Data property was wrapped in an envelope object (e.g. data.items rather than data)
diagnostic_checks: Inspect Array.isArray(value) immediately before the map invocation
Check server response shape in network dev tools or logs
suggested_resolutions: Initialize state with an empty array: useState([])
Use defensive fallback: (Array.isArray(items) ? items : []).map(...)
Unwrap the array correctly from response envelopes (e.g. response.data.items)

title: Node.js Module Not Found (MODULE_NOT_FOUND)
explanation: Node.js module resolver failed to locate the specified module in node_modules or relative file paths.
possible_causes: Package is listed in package.json but 'npm install' or 'pnpm install' has not been run
Relative path typo (e.g. missing './' or wrong file extension)
Package installed in a parent or sibling directory outside workspace scope
diagnostic_checks: Verify node_modules directory exists in the project root
Check package.json dependencies for the required package name
suggested_resolutions: Run 'npm install' or 'yarn install' in the project root
Verify relative path starts with './' or '../' when importing local files
Check case sensitivity if running on Linux CI environments

title: Network Connection Refused (ECONNREFUSED)
explanation: The target machine or port actively refused the TCP connection request because no service is listening on that address.
possible_causes: The downstream service (database, cache, mock server) is not running
Service is listening on a different port than configured in the client
Binding mismatch: service is bound to 127.0.0.1 (IPv4) but client contacted localhost (resolving to ::1 IPv6)
Docker container port mapping is missing or incorrect
diagnostic_checks: Check if service process is active using 'Get-Service', 'docker ps', or 'netstat -ano'
Verify connection using 'curl http://127.0.0.1:<port>' or 'Test-NetConnection'
suggested_resolutions: Start the required database, daemon, or server process
Use explicit '127.0.0.1' instead of 'localhost' to prevent IPv4/IPv6 ambiguity
Verify environment variables (e.g. PORT, DB_HOST, DB_PORT) match service configuration

title: Missing Environment Configuration Variable
explanation: Application startup failed because a required environment variable was not supplied in the environment or .env file.
possible_causes: The developer did not copy .env.example to .env upon initial setup
Environment variable name mismatch or casing discrepancy
Process execution runner did not load the .env file
diagnostic_checks: Check whether .env file exists in the current working directory
Verify environment variable is present via os.environ or process.env
suggested_resolutions: Create .env from .env.example and populate required keys
Use python-dotenv or dotenv-cli to load environment variables before launch
Supply sensible fallback defaults in configuration schemas where appropriate

title: Test Assertion Failure
explanation: A test assertion evaluated to False because actual output differed from expected behavior.
possible_causes: Underlying business logic bug introduced in recent change
Stale test expectations not updated after an intended contract modification
Non-deterministic test state or shared database pollution between test runs
diagnostic_checks: Review the diff between actual and expected values in test output
Run the failing test in isolation to check for state leakage across tests
suggested_resolutions: Debug the source code where actual value diverged from expected specification
Update test expectation if the behavior change was deliberate and approved
Ensure test fixtures provide isolated, repeatable state

error_pattern: Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use <address>:<port>
title: Port Already In Use (EADDRINUSE)
explanation: A network server could not bind to the requested port because another active process is already listening on it.
possible_causes: A previous instance of the server was not properly terminated (orphan background process)
Another application or Docker container is bound to the same port
Rapid restart while the socket is in TIME_WAIT state without SO_REUSEADDR enabled
diagnostic_checks: Find the conflicting process with 'netstat -ano | findstr <port>' or 'lsof -i :<port>'
Check Task Manager or Activity Monitor for orphan node/python processes
suggested_resolutions: Terminate the conflicting process using 'Stop-Process -Id <PID>' or 'kill <PID>'
Configure the application to use an alternative port via environment variable (e.g. PORT=8001)
Gracefully handle SIGINT and SIGTERM in server lifecycle

error_pattern: ResolutionError: Conflicting dependencies found or incompatible package version
title: Dependency Version Conflict
explanation: The package manager could not satisfy transitive dependency version constraints across requested packages.
possible_causes: Two direct dependencies require mutually incompatible versions of a shared sub-dependency
Stale lockfile conflicting with updated manifest requirements
Installed Python or Node.js runtime version does not meet engine requirements
diagnostic_checks: Inspect dependency tree using 'pipdeptree' or 'npm ls'
Check package engine requirements against current runtime version
suggested_resolutions: Upgrade or pin compatible versions in pyproject.toml or package.json
Regenerate lockfile after clearing conflicting package entries
Use virtual environments or containerized environments with matched runtimes
